title: Count an insect’s body
hook: A familiar body has a repeatable layout.

doesNotKnow: Identify the basic adult insect body plan.

misconception: Any small jointed animal is an insect.
objective: Identify the basic adult insect body plan.

claims.text: A familiar body has a repeatable layout. A typical adult insect has which combination of main body regions and legs? The schematic has a head, thorax and abdomen, with three pairs of legs attached to the thorax. Typical adult insects have this basic body plan, though body parts and appendages can vary among insects.
claims.source: Source leads for independent checking: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, https://naturalhistory.si.edu/research/entomology; OpenStax Biology 2e, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/28-3-superphylum-ecdysozoa. The precise supporting passages have not been checked.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: A typical adult insect has three pairs of legs. How many legs is that? Three pairs contain six legs.
